issues.rationale: The subgroup-model criterion now requires treatment, age group, sex, both interactions, baseline HbA1c, and a site random effect while accepting mathematically equivalent hierarchical parameterizations.
The GLP-1 criterion now checks availability in both the trial and real-world sources and prohibits treating an absent or unsuitable field as an observed zero.
Checklist status and pass-rate calculations now use the original source evidence; corrected reconciled values may be reported separately but cannot erase a source-data failure.
Proposal A now requires numeric projected cycle-time results with a documented source-grounded calculation or scenario method rather than assumptions alone.
The rubric now accepts fully reconciled ledger/accrual or earned-settled methods and explicitly rejects double counting cancelled or pending commissions and their reversals.
Concentration analysis must now define its numerator, denominator, and negative-position treatment; coherent net-asset-value and gross-exposure methods remain acceptable.
The ROI baseline now requires the incident-log start and end dates or an equivalent unambiguous observation range in addition to the requested totals.

The former 12-weight compound row was split into atomic Proposal A outputs, assumptions, comparison, memo, workbook, presentation, and cross-deliverable consistency rows while preserving the task total weight.
The briefing must now include every factual divergence from the supervisor notes, while remaining free to prioritize the most consequential items in its narrative.

The defect is missing protocol, trial, mapping, and UCI source context in the evaluator. Adding hidden expected values to the rubric would violate the task-aligned design; the evaluator must receive canonical inputs or deterministic checks.

The rubric now confirms that an embedded Excel forest chart is valid without a separate image and accepts the adjacent estimates, confidence intervals, and interaction p-values as corroborating evidence of its visual contents.
The evaluator needs the dispute, billing, weather, rights, supervisor-note, and EIA sources. Hidden customer-level expected values were not added to compensate for absent references.

Complete discrepancy checking requires the CRM, ERP, customer master, checklist, and scan transcriptions. This belongs in evaluator inputs or deterministic comparison tooling, not hidden rubric answers.
The evaluator must receive the local data and benchmark extracts needed to validate triggers and calculations. No source-derived expected values were embedded in the rubric.
Conditional formatting and document pagination are explicit task requirements. Style inspection and page-aware rendering must be added to the evaluator rather than weakening the rubric.
Charts and rendered slide layouts require presentation rendering or chart extraction. The task's visual trade-off requirement remains valid and was not replaced with a hidden textual proxy.

Fee, position, volatility, retention, and clawback correctness require database, market, and external schedule inputs. These should be attached or checked deterministically rather than encoded as hidden answers.
The rubric content is aligned; validating Q3 metrics, schedule feasibility, instrument coverage, and memo evidence requires normalized local and external source extracts.

External-session color coding is an explicit deliverable requirement and the schedule already includes an Internal/External field. Workbook style inspection should verify the color instead of removing the requirement.
Employee-course states, schedules, survey evidence, OSHA citations, and ROI need the local and external sources. Hidden employee, course, or metric answers were not added.
Top-ten highlighting is an explicit workbook requirement, while rank and explanatory notes remain textually judgeable. Style-aware workbook inspection is required to verify the visual highlight.
